ai.literal: Lack of knowledge is the poverty among poverties; other lack, as poverty, the world will not consider.
ai.translation: The lack of knowledge is the poorest of all poverties; the world does not consider any other kind of deprivation to be true poverty.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாமையே வறுமைகளுள் மிகக் கொடிய வறுமையாகும்; மற்ற குறைபாடுகளை உலகம் வறுமையாகக் கருதாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate form of destitution as the lack of knowledge or wisdom. While people generally view the absence of material wealth as poverty, the author asserts that such material lack is not true poverty. The world does not regard other forms of deprivation as significant because they can be overcome or endured with effort. In contrast, a lack of understanding is a fundamental deficiency that renders a person truly helpless, regardless of what else they might possess.

ai.literal: An ignorant man rejoicing in heart giving is not anything else than the receiver's past merit.
ai.translation: When an ignorant man gives with a glad heart, it is due to nothing other than the past merit of the receiver.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவன் மனமகிழ்ந்து ஒரு கொடையைக் கொடுப்பது, அதனைப் பெறுகின்றவனுடைய தவப்பயனே தவிர வேறு ஒன்றும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the rare occurrence of an ignorant person performing an act of charity. Since an unwise person lacks the understanding to give purposefully, any instance where they give with a glad heart is not due to their own virtue. Instead, it is attributed entirely to the good fortune or past spiritual merit of the recipient. The word 'tavam' here refers to the accumulated merit or destiny of the receiver that makes the impossible happen.

ai.literal: Those who lack knowledge, themselves upon themselves inflicting harm, even for enemies doing is difficult.
ai.translation: The harm that those who lack wisdom inflict upon themselves is difficult even for their enemies to do to them.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் தமக்குத் தாமே செய்து கொள்ளும் துன்பத்தை, அவர்களுடைய பகைவர்களாலும் அவர்களுக்குச் செய்வது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the self-destructive nature of foolishness. People who lack wisdom constantly make poor decisions that bring suffering upon themselves. The poet emphasizes that the severity of this self-inflicted harm is so great that even their bitterest enemies would find it difficult to cause them such ruin. Ultimately, a foolish person's own ignorance acts as a far more destructive force than any external adversary.

ai.literal: Folly that which is called if you ask what, wisdom we possess we saying pride.
ai.translation: If you ask what constitutes true folly, it is the vanity of declaring, 'We possess great wisdom.'
ai.modern: அறியாமை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எதுவென்றால், 'நாங்கள் அறிவுடையவர்கள்' என்று தங்களைத் தாங்களே மதித்துக் கொள்ளும் செருக்கு ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the poet defines the essence of ignorance or folly. The word 'வெண்மை' literally means whiteness or blankness, which represents a blank, ignorant mind. Conversely, 'ஒண்மை' means brightness or clarity, representing wisdom. The poet explains that true ignorance is not merely a lack of knowledge, but the arrogant self-delusion ('செருக்கு') of believing oneself to be already wise, which shuts the door to all learning.

ai.literal: Behaving by undertaking things not learned, even that which one is thoroughly skilled in will bring doubt.
ai.translation: Pretending to practice what one has not learned will cast doubt even on the things one is truly skilled in.
ai.modern: தான் கற்காதவற்றை அறிந்தவர் போல மேற்கொண்டு நடப்பது, ஒருவன் குற்றமறக் கற்றுத் தேர்ந்தவற்றின் மீதும் மற்றவர்களுக்கு ஐயத்தை உண்டாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the folly of pretending to possess knowledge or skills that one has not actually learned. When a person falsely undertakes tasks beyond their knowledge, they expose their ignorance. This pretense is so damaging that it ruins their overall credibility. Consequently, even in fields where they are genuinely and flawlessly skilled, others will begin to look upon them with doubt and suspicion.

ai.literal: Indeed covering one's nakedness is foolishness, when the faults within themselves are not covered.
ai.translation: To cover one's physical nakedness is sheer foolishness when one does not cover or correct the moral faults within oneself.
ai.modern: தங்களிடம் உள்ள குற்றங்களை மறைக்காதபோது, உடலின் ஆடையற்ற தன்மையை மட்டும் மறைப்பது அறிவீனமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts physical nakedness with moral flaws. The word 'அற்றம்' refers to physical nakedness, which society expects one to cover with clothes. The poet argues that if a person does not cover or rectify the 'குற்றம்' (faults) within themselves ('தம்வயின்'), merely covering their physical body is 'புல்லறிவு' (petty knowledge or foolishness). True decency and wisdom lie in concealing or overcoming one's inner flaws rather than just wearing clothes to hide physical nakedness while leaving moral defects completely exposed.

ai.literal: A rare secret letting-slip knowledge-lacking-person will-do great-harm himself-indeed to-himself.
ai.translation: The ignorant man who lets a precious secret slip causes great harm to himself.
ai.modern: அரிய ரகசியங்களை வெளியில் சொல்லிவிடும் அறிவில்லாதவன், தனக்குத் தானே பெரும் துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்கிக் கொள்வான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the self-destructive behavior of an ignorant person. Such a person lacks the discretion to guard valuable or confidential information, represented here as 'அருமறை' (precious secret), and carelessly lets it slip out ('சோரும்'). By revealing what should be kept hidden, he brings immense trouble and ruin ('பெருமிறை') upon himself. The phrase 'தானே தனக்கு' emphasizes that the fool does not need an external enemy to destroy him; his own lack of wisdom is entirely sufficient to cause his downfall.

ai.literal: Even when commanded he does not do, himself he does not understand; that life, until the limit it departs, is a disease.
ai.translation: He will not do what he is instructed to do, nor does he know what to do on his own. Such a life is a disease to the world until the moment it departs.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் அறிவுறுத்தினாலும் செய்யமாட்டான்; தானாகவும் உணர்ந்து கொள்ளமாட்டான்; அவனுடைய உயிர் உடம்பை விட்டுப் போகும் வரை உலகிற்கு ஒரு நோயாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the height of ignorance (புல்லறிவாண்மை). A foolish person is one who neither listens to the wise advice of others nor possesses the self-awareness to act correctly on their own. The poet compares such an individual's very existence to a lingering disease. Until the day that person's life departs from their body, they remain a constant affliction and burden to those around them.

ai.literal: He who instructs an ignorant person himself does not see; the ignorant person becomes one who has understood only in the way he himself understands.
ai.translation: One who attempts to instruct an ignorant person is himself devoid of wisdom; and that ignorant person will only claim to have understood in his own limited, distorted way.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவனுக்கு அறிவுறுத்த முயல்பவன் தானும் அறிவில்லாதவன் ஆவான்; அந்த அறிவில்லாதவனோ தான் புரிந்து கொண்ட வழியிலேயே புரிந்து கொண்டதாகக் கொள்வான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of trying to teach someone who lacks the capacity or willingness to understand. The poet states that a person who attempts to instruct an ignorant person (காணாதான்) is himself acting without wisdom (தான் காணான்), as it is a pointless endeavor. Furthermore, the ignorant person will not grasp the true meaning of the instruction; instead, they will only interpret and believe they have understood it (கண்டானாம்) in their own flawed and limited way (தான் கண்ட ஆறு). Thus, true knowledge cannot be forced upon those who are unprepared to receive it.

ai.literal: He who says that which the people of the world say exists does not exist, will be considered as a ghost on the earth.
ai.translation: He who denies the existence of what the people of the world accept as real will be regarded as a demon on this earth.
ai.modern: உலக மக்கள் உண்டு என்று ஒப்புக்கொள்ளும் ஒன்றை இல்லை என்று கூறுபவன், இவ்வுலகில் ஒரு பேயாகக் கருதப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate foolishness of denying common consensus and established truths. When the collective wisdom of the world agrees that something exists or is true, a person who stubbornly denies it isolates himself from humanity. The poet uses the word 'அலகை' (ghost or demon) to describe such a denier, indicating that they are no longer considered part of human society. By refusing to align with the shared reality of the world, they walk among living humans like an alien, disembodied spirit.
